title: Eastern Express (Doğu Ekspresi) & Kars Winter Itinerary
seoTitle: Eastern Express (Doğu Ekspresi) & Kars Winter Itinerary
metaDescription: Plan the Eastern Express (Doğu Ekspresi) to Kars: Touristic vs regular train, ticket release timing, Ani Ruins, Lake Çıldır, and fly-one-way tips.
quickAnswer: The Touristic Eastern Express (Turistik Doğu Ekspresi) runs three times weekly between Ankara and Kars from December to March using private two-berth sleeper cabins and three-hour sightseeing halts. Take the train one way eastbound, spend three nights in Kars for Ani Ruins and frozen Lake Çıldır, and fly back to Istanbul.

body.text: How does the Touristic Eastern Express differ from the regular train?

The [TCDD Touristic Eastern Express](https://www.tcddtasimacilik.gov.tr/tr/turistik/detay/1) carries only private two-berth sleeper compartments and adds multi-hour daytime sightseeing stops along the 1,310-kilometre Ankara–Kars line, taking roughly 32 to 34 hours. The regular daily Doğu Ekspresi runs year-round in about 24 to 26 hours with reclining seats and four-berth couchettes, making brief station stops only.

Both trains cross the exact same snow-covered Anatolian gorges, including the dramatic Karasu River canyon near Erzincan. Your choice comes down to privacy, budget, and whether you want organised daylight halts in Erzincan, İliç, and Erzurum (eastbound) or Divriği and Sivas (westbound), as detailed in [Rail Turkey's Touristic Doğu Express guide](https://railturkey.org/travel/trains/mainline/doguturistik/).

body.text: How far in advance do sleeper tickets sell out?

Individual sleeper tickets on the [TCDD E-Bilet portal](https://ebilet.tcddtasimacilik.gov.tr/turistik-trenler/dogu-ekspresi) typically open 30 days before departure for regular trains—and 30 to 60 days ahead for seasonal Touristic departures—with peak January and February weekend cabins routinely selling out within minutes of going live online.

Because Turkish tour operators reserve a large block of Touristic carriages each winter, independent travellers have two realistic strategies: log into the TCDD app the exact morning your travel date opens (midweek departures sell out slower than Fridays), or check regularly for returned agency cancellations 10 to 14 days before departure. For broader cold-season routing across the country, read our [Türkiye in Winter travel guide](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/blog/turkey-in-winter-premium-travel-guide).
What should you see in Kars, Ani Ruins and Lake Çıldır?

Once you step off the train in Kars, budget three full days to explore the city's 19th-century Baltic basalt architecture, the medieval [UNESCO-listed Archaeological Site of Ani](https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/1518/) on the Armenian border, and a winter horse-drawn sleigh ride across frozen [Lake Çıldır](https://goturkiye.com/blog/keep-abreast-of-the-frozen-winter-lake-cildir).

items: Central Kars & Baltic Quarter: Walk the grid of black-basalt Russian-era mansions built after 1878, climb to Kars Castle for sunset over the Kümbet Mosque (Church of the Holy Apostles), and taste aged Kars gravyer cheese and roasted goose (kaz eti).

[Ani Ruins](https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/1518/): Standing 42 kilometres east of Kars beside the Arpaçay gorge bordering Armenia, this former Bagratid capital rewards half a day with a knowledgeable local guide—covered in depth in our [Ani Ruins & Lake Çıldır 3-day route](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/blog/ani-ruins-kars).

[Lake Çıldır](https://goturkiye.com/blog/keep-abreast-of-the-frozen-winter-lake-cildir): Roughly 75 kilometres northeast of Kars, Eastern Anatolia's largest freshwater lake freezes thick enough in midwinter for horse-drawn sleigh rides and ice-fishing lunches of yellow carp (sarı balık).

body.text: Can you fly one way and take the train the other?

Yes—and flying one way is by far the smartest way to build an Eastern Express winter itinerary. Ride the train eastbound from Ankara to Kars for the anticipation and snowy gorge daylight, then fly straight back from [Kars Harakani Airport (KSY)](https://dhmi.gov.tr/sayfalar/havalimani/kars/GenelBilgiler.aspx) to Istanbul or Ankara in roughly two hours.

Taking the train in both directions burns nearly three full days inside a compartment and repeats the same corridor. If eastbound Touristic tickets are sold out for your dates, reverse the pattern: fly into Kars first, spend three nights exploring Ani and Lake Çıldır, and catch the westbound Touristic train back to Ankara—which includes a coveted three-hour stop for the UNESCO-listed Great Mosque of Divriği.

faq.q: Does the Eastern Express depart from Istanbul or Ankara?
faq.a: The Eastern Express departs from Ankara Gar. Travellers starting in Istanbul take the YHT high-speed train from Söğütlüçeşme to Ankara (about 4.5 hours) and transfer at Ankara Station.

faq.q: Is food included on the Touristic Eastern Express?
faq.a: No, meals are not included in the rail ticket. The train has a dining car serving simple Turkish dishes, and most experienced passengers also bring thermoses, fruit, cheese, and snacks for their private cabin.

faq.q: Are there showers on the Touristic Eastern Express?
faq.a: No. Sleeper cabins include two convertible beds, a small washbasin, a mini-fridge, power outlets, and heating, while toilets are shared at the end of each carriage.

faq.q: How cold does Kars get during the Eastern Express season?
faq.a: January and February highs in Kars often sit between -5°C and -2°C, with overnight lows dropping below -15°C. Pack thermal base layers, insulated waterproof boots, gloves, and a windproof parka.

faq.q: Are the sightseeing excursions included in the Touristic train ticket?
faq.a: No. TCDD covers the rail transport and scheduled three-hour station stops; local bus excursions at Erzincan, İliç, Erzurum, or Divriği are paid separately on board or arranged independently.

faq.q: How far is Kars Harakani Airport from central Kars?
faq.a: Kars Harakani Airport (KSY) sits only six kilometres south of the city centre, taking 10 to 15 minutes by taxi even in snowy winter conditions.
